## Natural history notes

A small reddish-brown invasive ant characterized by its painful sting, aggressive swarming behavior, and mound-building colonies in open soil. In Florida, it is common in lawns, pastures, roadsides, fields, parks, agricultural areas, and disturbed habitats, especially in sunny areas with moist or recently disturbed ground. It feeds on insects, seeds, honeydew, carrion, and other small food sources, and large colonies can affect native arthropods, ground-nesting wildlife, livestock, pets, and people through predation and repeated stings.
